properties.chose:
Option (C), on Anthony's word of 2026-10-13: "agree with C. however, C sounds a lot like how git works. Can we do a quick search of the design for what we've discussed on git and how to measure change?"

The search found that the design already holds most of git's machinery, so (C) is built ON it:
- per-item lineage (cap:lineage-is-kept-per-item, verified): every node and edge carries its content hash and the hash of the version it replaced;
- the fork-point coordinate (dec:fork-point-address, accepted 2026-07-24): a release's epoch carries the export's content hash as identity, and git supplies the bytes. A reflow2-native ref or branch layer was rejected then;
- the open question of what identifies a release's snapshot (dec:what-pins-a-snapshot, 2026-07-30), whose suggested shape is the content hash as identity and the git tag as address.

So (C) adds no refs, branches or second history. Each cut records the status of every intent node on the release, stored as a delta from the previous release's snapshot, inside the graph, so a design hosted on flo2.io with no git copy is counted too. The snapshot is identified by the epoch's content hash, as the fork point already is. Past releases are back-filled from the design copy committed at each tag, diffed item by item through the per-item lineage, where a copy exists; a release with no copy is named as having none.

Not chosen: (A), which undercounts (it reads "0 dropped" where 11 were), and (B), which can come later if it matters which change took a requirement away. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.decision:
For req:a-changelog-shows-what-was-taken-away-beside-what-was-added. The window between two releases is the epochs between them, and changelog_view counts only the ChangeEvents pinned there. MEASURED 2026-10-13 on reflow2's own design (origin/main after the 0.83.5 cut, 7,206 nodes):
- A status move is not a change. CHANGED edges record an action (added, modified or removed) and never a status before and after. The 11 dropped and 5 deferred requirements, and the 32 superseded and 6 rejected decisions, are on the time axis nowhere as the move that took them away.
- Additions are mostly invisible too. 44 of 383 requirements were ever recorded as "added" by a change.
- No date stands in. The core takes no clock. AUTHORED_BY carries authored_at or approved_at on about 1,080 of 1,440 edges, but a release and its epoch carry no date (2 of 308 epochs have created_at), and the 801 snapshots carry none either.
- Pinning is uneven: recent cuts pin 1 or 2 changes, while older cuts pinned up to 55.
- Failures: 0 of 441 checks have ever recorded a failed run, and 153 changes are test_failure_fix.

OPTIONS:
(A) COUNT WHAT THE WINDOW ALREADY RECORDS: the pinned changes' added and removed by node type, plus change types (deprecation, requirement_creep, test_failure_fix). It is cheap, but it would read "0 dropped" where 11 were dropped, which is the false reassurance the measure exists to prevent.
(B) RECORD EVERY STATUS MOVE AS A CHANGE. set_requirement_status, set_decision_status, set_capability_status and set_verification_status each write a small ChangeEvent with CHANGED {action, field: status, from, to}, as set_artifact_checksums already writes chg:accept-*. The cut pins the increment's changes as it does now. Counts are complete going forward. It adds one node per status move, still depends on the cut pinning everything, and history stays invisible.
(C) EACH RELEASE KEEPS A STATUS SNAPSHOT. The cut records, on the release, every intent node's status (requirements, capabilities, decisions, checks). The balance is the difference between two releases' snapshots.
  - It needs no clock and no pinning.
  - To stay small, it is stored as a delta from the previous release's snapshot, with the first one whole.
  - Past releases can be back-filled from the design copy committed at each tag, where one exists. Otherwise the line says that release has no snapshot.
  - Limit: it counts the net move between two cuts. A requirement added and dropped inside one window appears in neither column, and the line says so.
  - Failures: checks whose status moved to failing between snapshots, plus the window's pinned test_failure_fix changes.

RECOMMENDED: (C). It is the only option that is complete for any design, hosted or local, without depending on every session pinning and dating its changes. It adds one record per cut, not one per status move.

Counter-arguments:
- (C) cannot say which change took a requirement away, only that it went between two releases. (B) could; the two are not exclusive, and (B) can come later if the "which" matters.
- A design that never cuts releases gets no balance from (C). Such a design has no release-to-release changelog either.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-13 — the changelog's balance line counts from a status snapshot each release keeps (option C), built on the design's existing git-like machinery rather than beside it
properties.rationale: Asked after Anthony chose the balance line's place (changelog_view) on 2026-10-13, because how it is counted decides whether the line is objective. Counting only what the window records today would report removals as zero when they are only unrecorded. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
